digital-nomad.label: Digital nomad visas
digital-nomad.desc: Visas designed for remote workers earning foreign income. 30+ countries now offer them in 2026.

passive-income.label: Passive income visas
passive-income.desc: Visas for retirees, rentiers and passive income earners. No remote work or local employment required.

investor.label: Investor and golden visas
investor.desc: Long-term residency in exchange for investment or bank deposit. Path to citizenship in some.

freelance.label: Freelance and self-employment visas
freelance.desc: Visas for liberal professions and self-employed workers. Local clients usually allowed.

cost.introTpl: What it actually costs to live in {name} as a remote worker in 2026 — rent, food, coworking, transport and the monthly total for a solo nomad, a couple and a family.
cost.tiersIntro: The single monthly figure hides a lot. Here is what the same city costs at three different lifestyles.
cost.leanDesc: Shared flat or a studio outside the centre, cooking most meals, working from home and cafés, public transport only.
cost.comfortDesc: Your own one-bedroom in a good neighbourhood, eating out several times a week, a coworking membership, the occasional taxi.
cost.premiumDesc: Central apartment, restaurants most nights, a dedicated desk rather than a hot desk, gym and regular weekend trips.
cost.methodTpl: Figures are 2026 estimates built from the {name} cost index ({index}/100), cross-referenced against Numbeo and Nomad List reporting and adjusted for what remote workers actually spend. Real prices move with neighbourhood, season and lifestyle, so treat this as a baseline to adjust rather than a quote.

faq.q: How much does it cost to live in {name}?
faq.a: A solo digital nomad should budget around ${total} per month all-in for {name} in 2026. That covers a one-bedroom flat in the centre, utilities, internet, groceries, some eating out, a coworking desk and public transport. A couple runs closer to ${couple} and a family of four around ${family}.

With a cost index of {index} out of 100, {name} sits {position}. The single biggest lever is rent: ${rent} per month in the centre versus ${rentOut} just outside it. Moving one neighbourhood out is usually worth more than every other saving combined.

Expect about ${rent} a month for a one-bedroom apartment in the city centre of {name}, or roughly ${rentOut} outside the centre. Short lets aimed at nomads are typically priced above these figures, so a longer commitment is where the savings are.

faq.q: Can you live in {name} on a tight budget?
faq.a: Yes — a lean month in {name} comes in near ${lean}. That means a room in a shared flat or a studio away from the centre, cooking most meals, working from home and cafés rather than a coworking space, and sticking to public transport.

faq.q: How much do you need per month to live comfortably in {name}?
faq.a: Comfortable in {name} lands around ${total} a month: your own one-bedroom in a decent area, eating out a few times a week, a coworking membership and no real thought before booking a taxi. Push to roughly ${premium} and you are into central-apartment, restaurants-most-nights territory.
